summary: Redwood AE+SE demo of hosted embeddings + rerank endpoints for Blueleaf. Customer is evaluating options to improve search relevance for product and doc search; key concerns: latency at scale, cost per embedding, vector index size, and SOC2/KMS compliance. Agreed to run a short pilot with sample dataset and benchmark scripts; Redwood to send pricing and rerank templates.
transcript: Meeting header: 2027-03-15 14:00 UTC | Duration: 45m | Attendees: Maya, Ethan, Jonas (Redwood) — Lena, Dev, Samir (Blueleaf)
[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intro — I'm Maya, AE at Redwood, and with me is Ethan our SE. how are you all?
[00:10] Lena: Good, thanks. excited to see how embeddings + rerank could help improve our site search

[00:18] Ethan: Great. we'll walk through the hosted API flow: embeddings ingestion, approximate nearest neighbor search, and then the rerank call which re-scores top candidates with a small cross-encoder model.
[00:35] Dev: quick Q — are we doing vector store managed by Redwood or do we push vectors to our index?
[00:42] Maya: good question. for hosted API we can store vectors in Redwood-managed indexes (we handle storage/ops), or you can push vectors to your own store and call rerank — both supported
[00:55] Samir: what's the billing model for hosted vectors? per-embedding or storage?

[01:02] Maya: embeddings billed per embedding call + optional storage cost for long-term retention; we'll send detailed pricing. sample: 1536-d embeddings at $0.0004 per vector (example), storage depends on retention tier
[01:20] Lena: and latency — we need sub-200ms for user searches ideally, is that realistic with rerank?

[01:30] Ethan: so there are two hops: ANN search (nearest neighbors) which is fast, and rerank which calls a small model to re-score top-k. typical hosted rerank latencies are 80–160ms depending on k and payload size; we can tune k and batch size to meet 200ms SLO
[01:52] Dev: are we able to run rerank on a smaller quantized model to save cost?
[01:58] Ethan: yes, we have model variants — smaller re-rankers (quantized) and larger ones for quality. Redwood Optimize will provide recommendations based on your query distribution
[02:12] Jonas: small note, the transcript's auto-captions sometimes change acronyms — 'K V cache' showed earlier, that's 'KV cache' in the runtime docs
[02:20] Samir: security: we need SOC 2 and KMS integration, plus audit logs for vectors and requests. can hosted API satisfy that?

[02:30] Maya: yes, we support SOC 2, KMS integrations, and audit logs; for stricter controls we offer Dedicated or Private deployments. but many customers use hosted with customer-managed KMS via BYOK
[02:47] Dev: data retention — if we upload documents and embeddings, can we set retention policies?
[02:52] Ethan: absolutely; retention is configurable per-index. we also support immediate deletion APIs and audit trails
[03:05] Lena: demo time? would love to see a live example with our sample queries

[03:12] Ethan: sure — I'm going to share my screen — running a small demo dataset. first, we call the embeddings endpoint with a batch of docs. note: we use continuous batching and prefix caching for hot prefixes to reduce per-token cost — sometimes the transcription calls it 'prefix cashing' which is a small auto-correction

[03:40] [screen share] Ethan: here is the POST /v1/embeddings call. payload has an array of texts, we set batch_size 128. response returns vectors and ids. we'll then upsert to an index and call /v1/ann/search to get top 100 candidates
[04:10] Ethan: now calling /v1/rerank with the query + candidate ids. rerank returns re-scored list with explainability tokens (score, match highlights). see the difference vs raw ANN ordering
[04:35] Lena: wow the rerank fixed a bunch of false positives for product synonyms — that's promising
[04:42] Dev: what's the cost of a rerank call per request?
[04:47] Maya: depends on model size & k. example: small re-ranker $0.001 per rerank call at k=10, medium $0.004. we'll put exact numbers in the pricing doc
[05:05] Samir: about scale — we have ~2M docs, how does index size and search latency change?

[05:14] Ethan: ANN scales sub-linearly but index size matters for memory/IO. for ~2M docs we recommend sharded indexes or using vector compression/quantization. Redwood Optimize will flag when to switch to Dedicated for throughput
[05:35] Dev: if we want to keep vectors in our own Pinecone cluster, can we still use Redwood rerank?

[05:40] Ethan: yes, you can host vectors elsewhere and call our rerank API with candidate ids and texts. the rerank stage is stateless and just needs the candidates' text or embeddings depending on the flow
[05:55] Lena: any best practices on candidate selection k? we want recall high but keep latency low
[06:03] Ethan: a common pattern: ANN k=100 to max recall, rerank top-10 with cross-encoder. if latency is tight, tune ANN k down or use a smaller reranker and tune thresholding
[06:20] Dev: are there SDKs? we prefer node/python clients
[06:24] Maya: yes, we have SDKs and quickstart templates. I'll include the repo links in the follow-up
[06:33] Samir: compliance checklist — can you share SOC2 and encryption docs?
[06:37] Maya: yes, security pack is in our docs; we'll share the SOC2 report and KMS integration guide
[06:47] Lena: what about A/B testing and rollout? we need to run a canary with partial traffic
[06:53] Ethan: built-in route-based rollouts let you divert x% of traffic to a new reranker, with telemetry in Console. you can compare CTR/ESR and rollback automatically if quality drops
[07:10] Dev: curious about cold-start for new docs — how soon are embeddings searchable after ingestion?
[07:16] Ethan: ingestion typically completes within seconds to a minute depending on batching. near-real-time indexing is supported, and we can provide hooks for post-upsert consistency checks
[07:30] [minor crosstalk] Lena: sorry one more — does rerank support structured fields (e.g., product category) to boost results?
[07:38] Ethan: yes, you can include metadata in the rerank input to bias scores, and we support hybrid scoring with BM25 signals

[07:50] Maya: quick note on cost optimization — using lower-dim embeddings, caching hot queries, and batching at ingestion massively reduce unit costs. Redwood Optimize gives suggestions automatically
[08:05] Lena: sounds good. what's the pilot look like?

[08:10] Maya: recommended: 1) customer shares random sample ~20k docs + query log, 2) Redwood runs one-week benchmark with ANN + rerank variations, 3) measure latency, relevance (MRR/CTR), and cost. we'll present results and recommendations
[08:25] Dev: timeline? we want to ship improvements in Q2
[08:29] Maya: if we start next week we can complete the pilot in 7–10 days and then iterate; sounds feasible for Q2
[08:40] Samir: ok let's do it. any blockers on legal?
[08:44] Maya: we'll share procurement and SOC2 docs; if you require a DPA or specific TOS changes we'll loop Legal — typical lead time depends on redlines
[08:55] Lena: great. can you also show a sample rerank prompt?
[09:00] Ethan: yes i'll paste a couple templates in the follow-up — short cross-encoder prompt and a version with metadata boosts
[09:10] Jonas: I'll capture action items. quick note: transcript may have some mis-typed model names, e.g., 'Redwood Optimize' got cut to 'Redwood opt' in automated notes
[09:20] Maya: perfect. to recap — Redwood will send pricing, security docs, SDK links, and rerank templates. Blueleaf will share sample dataset and queries. schedule follow-up deep-dive next week
[09:35] Lena: thanks everyone — excited to see the results
[09:38] Meeting end
